column2: If it’s very thick, add boiled water until it runs off the spoon for your baby.
Stir in the olive oil and serve lukewarm.
Wash leafy vegetables such as leek and spinach thoroughly; limit spinach to 1–2 times a week.
24 hours in the fridge; reheat once and discard the rest.
Red lentil and vegetable mash
Half a cup grated vegetables (your choice)
1.5 cups drinking water
1 teaspoon butter or olive oil
A pinch of cumin, if you like
Wash the lentils until the water runs clear.
Put the lentils, vegetables and water in a pot; once boiling, skim off the foam.
Cook over a low heat, stirring occasionally, for 20–25 minutes until the lentils break down.
Mash with a fork or blender, thinning with boiled water if needed.
Add the oil and optional cumin and give lukewarm.
Legumes can cause wind; start with 2–3 spoonfuls the first time.
24 hours in the fridge; can be frozen for 1 month.
Oat and vegetable mash
2 tablespoons fine rolled oats
3 tablespoons grated vegetables (your choice)
1 cup drinking water
Grate the vegetables and put them in a pot with the water.
Once boiling, cook for 7–8 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Add the oats and cook 4–5 more minutes, stirring constantly, until thick.
Remove from the heat and add the olive oil; mash or purée according to your baby’s age.
Serve once lukewarm.
Oats may carry gluten cross-contamination; if coeliac disease is suspected, consult your doctor.
Best eaten straight away; at most 24 hours in the fridge.
Rice and vegetable dish
Half a cup finely chopped vegetables (your choice)
1 teaspoon butter
Soak the rice in lukewarm water for 15 minutes and drain.
Put the vegetables and water in a pot; once boiling, add the rice.
Cook covered over a low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Stir in the butter and leave to steam for 5 minutes.
Mash it or give it lightly mashed with some texture, according to your baby’s chewing skills.
Vary the grains; rather than rice every day, rotate with bulgur, oats and other grains.
Cool rice dishes quickly and keep them in the fridge for no more than 24 hours.
Bulgur and vegetable dish
Gently heat the olive oil in a pot, add the vegetables and toss for 3 minutes.
Add the water; once boiling, add the bulgur.
Cook covered over a low heat for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Remove from the heat and leave to steam for 10 minutes.
Lightly mash with a fork and serve lukewarm.
If you use tomato, peel it and remove the seeds.
24 hours in a sealed container in the fridge.
Half a cup boiled or roasted vegetables (your choice)
2 tablespoons full-fat plain yogurt
A few dill leaves, if you like
Cook the vegetables until soft: steam for 10–12 minutes or roast at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Mash the vegetables well with a fork and cool to room temperature.
Add the yogurt and stir until smooth.
Add the olive oil and finely chopped dill.
Don’t add yogurt to hot vegetables; let them cool so it doesn’t curdle.
If there is a history of dairy allergy, consult your doctor.
Eat the yogurt mixture the same day.
Vegetable sauté with egg
3 tablespoons finely chopped vegetables (your choice)
Melt the butter in a small pan, add the vegetables and soften, covered, for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg in a separate bowl and pour it over the vegetables.
Over a low heat, stir constantly until the egg is fully cooked; no runny part should remain.
Let it cool and break into small pieces or mash with a fork.
Always give babies fully cooked egg.
Eat straight away; don’t leave it to stand.
Chicken and vegetable dish
50 g chicken breast
Without washing the chicken, dice it small on a separate chopping board.
Put the chicken in a pot with the water; once boiling, skim off the foam and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the potato and vegetables and cook for 15–20 minutes, until the chicken is white inside and the fibres separate easily.
Add the olive oil; mash or finely shred according to age.
Serve lukewarm.
There should be no pink left inside the chicken.
Wash your hands and the worktop after touching raw chicken.
Mince and vegetable dish
2 tablespoons lean beef mince
1 tablespoon grated tomato
Heat the olive oil, add the mince and fry, breaking it up to avoid lumps, until it changes colour.
Add the tomato and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables and water; cook covered over a low heat for 20 minutes until the vegetables are very soft.
Mash as appropriate for age and let it cool.
For iron, serve mince dishes together with vegetables containing vitamin C.
Chickpea and vegetable mash
3 tablespoons boiled chickpeas (skins removed)
Half a cup boiled vegetables (your choice)
2–3 tablespoons cooking water
Soak the chickpeas overnight; the next day change the water and boil for 60–70 minutes until very soft.
Slip the skins off the chickpeas with your fingers.
Steam the vegetables separately for 12–15 minutes.
Mash the chickpeas and vegetables smoothly with the cooking water.
Add the olive oil and serve lukewarm.
Whole chickpeas are a choking hazard; always give them mashed.
48 hours in the fridge; can be frozen for 1 month.
Haricot bean and vegetable dish
3 tablespoons boiled haricot beans
Soak the haricot beans overnight, discard the water and boil for 60 minutes until soft.
Cook the tomato in olive oil for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables, beans and water and cook over a low heat for 20 minutes.
Mash thoroughly with a fork or blend so the bean skins break down.
When giving dried legumes for the first time, start with 1–2 spoonfuls.
48 hours in the fridge.
Fish and vegetable mash
50 g boneless salmon or sea bass fillet
Half a cup chopped vegetables (your choice)
A few drops of lemon juice (optional)
Feel the fish with your fingertips and check for bones one by one.
Steam the vegetables for 10 minutes, then add the fish and steam for 8–10 minutes more.
Remove from the heat when the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Mash the fish and vegetables with the olive oil and make sure again that no bones remain.
Choose salmon, sea bass or sea bream rather than large fish high in mercury (shark, swordfish).
Roasted vegetable mash
1 cup roughly chopped vegetables (your choice)
A pinch of thyme (optional)
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil and thyme and spread on a tray lined with baking paper.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, until a fork goes in easily.
When lukewarm, mash with a fork, or after 12 months give as soft finger-sized pieces.
Roasting brings out the vegetables’ natural sweetness; there’s no need to add sugar.
Mini meatballs with vegetables
100 g lean beef mince
3 tablespoons grated, squeezed vegetables (your choice)
2 tablespoons breadcrumbs or rolled oats
A pinch of cumin
